parts.title: Reading - Part 3
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer.
parts.passage_text:
I've just come back from a summer camp I did in Scotland and I'd like to tell you about it. It was my very first holiday without my family so I was a little worried at first. My mother drove me to the airport early in the morning and by quarter to seven I was on the plane by myself.

The flight lasted one hour and a half. During the journey, I made friends with another girl, Ida, who was going to the same summer camp. She was from Denmark but her English was quite good. When we arrived, we found a young lady waiting for us just outside the airport.

The summer camp only lasted twelve days, but I did so many things that it seemed much longer. In the morning we could do different activities: I really enjoy art so I chose a drawing course and improved my cartoon drawing skills. We also did sports I often do, like horse riding, table tennis and football. Ida also asked me to join the guitar course so now I can play a few songs.

When I came back a few days ago I was glad to see my family again, but I was also a little sad because I was going to miss my new friends from the summer camp. Anyway, Ida and I text each other every day and she promised she will visit me next month.

questions.question: How did Emma feel about leaving?

options.A: a bit scared about travelling alone
options.B: glad that she was going to a new country
options.C: bored because she didn't like travelling by plane

questions.question: What did Emma do during the journey?

options.A: She chatted with her best friend, who was going to the same summer camp.
options.B: She started talking to somebody on the plane.
options.C: She met a young lady who worked at the airport.

questions.question: How long did Emma's stay at the summer camp?
Which new things did Emma learn at the summer camp?
What's Emma planning to do in the future?

options.A: She's going to a summer camp again next summer.
options.B: She's going to text her new friend every day.
options.C: She's going to meet Ida soon.

parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct picture.

questions.question: What time does Greta have her tennis match?
questions.transcript:
Greta: Mum, are you going to your chess course?
Mum: Yes, it's at quarter to three. Why?
Greta: I'm playing tennis with Martha this afternoon. Could you give me a lift to the court before your course? I need to be there by twenty past two.
Mum: Oh, OK then, but let's hurry up: it's already ten to two!

questions.question: What will Tom do next Tuesday?
questions.transcript:
Girl: Have you been to the new swimming pool? It's really cool! I went there on Saturday.
Girl: Great! Why don't we go there together next Tuesday afternoon, Tom?
Tom: I'd love to but I have a guitar lesson on that day. If you want, we can go with Katie on Thursday, if she doesn't have her dance class?
Girl: OK I'll ask Katie, then.

questions.question: What did the girl do yesterday?

options_descriptions.B: Invitation to Mandy's Party (Wednesday at 6 p.m.)

Girl: I wanted to, but I had a French test this morning so I had to study all afternoon. What did you do yesterday?
Boy: I went to a restaurant with my family. We wanted to celebrate my grandma's birthday.

questions.question: How's the boy going home from the station tomorrow?
questions.transcript:
Boy: I don't know how to get home from the station tomorrow evening. The buses stop early.
Emma: Isn't your dad going to pick you up?
Boy: Unfortunately, he'll be at work, and my mother isn't in town.
Emma: Don't worry. I'll ask my brother: he's having dinner with my aunt tomorrow. She lives near the station. I'm sure he can meet you there and drive you home.
Boy: Thanks, Emma.

questions.question: What is the girl going to eat?
questions.transcript:
Boy: Have you decided what you want? The chicken is very good.
Girl: Mmm, I'd like to have something light. I'm playing volleyball this afternoon.
Boy: How about fruit salad? I tried it yesterday for dessert and it tasted delicious.
Girl: Actually, I don't really like having sweet foods for lunch. I think I'll try the fish soup.
Boy: I'll have chicken again.

parts.title: Listening - Part 2
parts.instructions: For each question, write the correct answer in the gap. Write one word or a number or a date or a time.
parts.context: You will hear a teacher telling her students about a museum they are going to visit.
parts.transcript:
Good Morning, I'm going to tell you what you need to know for next Friday's trip to the Egyptian Museum. First of all, remember that students pay less than adults, so instead of the usual 8 pounds you will only need to bring 5 pounds fifty; if your parents want to go too, they will have to pay the full price.
You will go to the museum with the history teacher but he's ill so you can't give him the money. The Maths teacher will collect it tomorrow at the end of her lesson.
The Museum opens at half past nine, but we'll have to leave school and be at the bus station by quarter past eight because the journey there is about 45 minutes. We won't take the train because it would take longer to get there.
The Museum has a café so you don't need to bring food or drink. Remember that you can take photos inside the museum so don't leave your cameras at home.

parts.title: Listening - Part 3
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer.
parts.context: You will hear Frank talking about a holiday he had.

questions.question: Where did Frank go?
How long did it take to get there?
Where did Frank stay?
Frank thinks the holiday was
Where's Frank going next year?

parts.transcript:
Girl: Hi Frank, I hear you've just come back. How was your holiday?
Frank: It was amazing! I've always loved going to the beach or visiting other countries in summer, but the two weeks I spent in the mountains were absolutely brilliant.
Girl: I'd love to go too. Is it far from here?
Frank: No, actually it's quite close, just half an hour by car. There's a wonderful hotel with tennis courts and an indoor swimming pool. I'm sure you would love it.
Girl: Cool! Did you stay there?
Frank: Unfortunately I couldn't. It was fully booked; there was a nice campsite near the hotel but it was too cold; anyway, my father's best friend lives there, so we stayed there all the time.
Girl: I'm really glad you had a great time… what was the weather like?
Frank: It was mostly sunny and warm. I was afraid it would rain a lot: you know it may be a little boring when it rains in the mountains. I hope next time we'll stay longer. Two weeks isn't enough!
Girl: You mean you're going there again next year?
Frank: Actually, my parents told me they'd like to do something different next summer. They love visiting foreign towns so we'll see what to do before June.
Girl: That's the best thing to do. There's still a lot of time before next summer.

questions.question: You will hear two friends talking about what they will do tomorrow. What will the weather be like?
questions.transcript:
Boy: Shall we go for a bike ride tomorrow?
Girl: I don't know. I think it might rain tomorrow…
Boy: No, I don't think so. The weather forecast said it's definitely going to be sunny.
Girl: OK, let's try it. The last time we went, it started raining while we were cycling, but it stopped after a few minutes.
Boy: Right, see you tomorrow then!

parts.title: Listening - Part 5
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer.
parts.context: You will hear Harriet talking to her aunt about a school concert. What will each classmate do?
parts.transcript:
Harriet: Are you coming to our school concert on Saturday, Aunt Milly?
Milly: Sure, Harriet. Are you playing the piano again?
Harriet: No, I'm singing a song from 'Rigoletto'.
Milly: The opera?
Harriet: Yes. I love opera! This year we're including different types of music. Akos is singing hip-hop.
Milly: So, everyone is singing or playing an instrument?
Harriet: No. If a student doesn't want to go on stage, they can help with the show.
Milly: I remember Olga filmed last year's show.
Harriet: Yes, but now she's learning the guitar, so she's doing that this year.
Milly: So, no one's filming the show this year?
Harriet: Oh yes. Shane has broken his arm so he's doing the filming.
Milly: And your sister Jenny?
Harriet: She wanted to organise the tickets, but our teacher is doing that. So Jenny's doing the lights.
Milly: Oh, OK! And what about Tracy? She loves playing drums, doesn't she?
Harriet: Yes, but she's so noisy she has to play the violin instead.
Milly: Ha ha! OK, so where can I get a ticket from?
